title: The Best Matter Door and Window Sensors
subtitle: Matter-over-Thread contact sensors for every major platform.
intro: Matter door and window sensors run over Thread, so every one here needs a Thread border router. There are only a few on Amazon so far. We scored them on rating, review volume, and features.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

scoring.review_age_weighting: Listings under 24 months old with at least 30 reviews have their review count multiplied by min(2, 24 / age in months, age floored at 6) before scoring; older listings are unchanged. Listing age is Amazon's Date First Available, or an estimate from the ASIN when the listing does not show it.

avoid.name: arre Contact Sensor with Matter and Thread, Works with Apple Home, Google Home and SmartThings, Door/Garage Sensor
avoid.verdict: The listing is a list of logos: no battery type, no battery life, no size, and no mounting details.
reasons: Each bullet is a single phrase like "Works with Apple Home" with no specifications.
Battery type, battery life, and size aren't listed anywhere.
The Aqara P2 costs less and has a real listing and over a thousand reviews.

buyers_guide.q: How do door and window sensors work?
buyers_guide.a: A magnet goes on the door or window and the sensor goes on the frame. When the two separate, the sensor reports open. Mount them within the gap the listing specifies, usually under an inch.

buyers_guide.q: How long do the batteries last?
buyers_guide.a: Most battery sensors on these lists are rated for one to three years, depending on how often they report. Low-power radios like Zigbee, Z-Wave, and Thread last much longer than Wi-Fi.

buyers_guide.q: Can I use these as a security system?
buyers_guide.a: They can trigger alerts and sirens through your smart home system, but they aren't a monitored alarm. For insurance discounts or police dispatch you need a professionally monitored system.
